acceptance_signals: A dated consumer-validation record names the current Codex host as the measured consumer and retains only normalized, repository-safe facts.

The record proves the configured AgentGov server is enabled, the project allow-list and current callable surface both contain the same six named tools, and the current journey successfully exercises proposal form, alignment start/update/resolve, and post-change self-review start/complete.

The record compares that measured six-tool host binding with the source contract of six base tools and eight form-capable tools, classifies completion and drift review as host-configured omissions, and does not label them Adapter failures.
No Codex configuration, AgentGov runtime behavior, user configuration, external consumer repository, Git state, release, publication, or deployment is changed.
A deterministic documentation test protects the measured facts, privacy boundary, official OpenAI documentation reference, and explicit unknowns; focused and full repository validation pass.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-0378bf5dc5dd48d1b61ba598204869d3 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Record one privacy-bounded, reproducible compatibility observation for the current real Codex MCP consumer: confirm the enabled AgentGov server, compare the project six-tool allow-list with the current callable tool surface and the source eight-tool contract, exercise the admitted six-tool journey through native proposal, alignment, and post-change self-review calls, and document the exact host-configuration gap without changing AgentGov behavior or Codex configuration.

items: A live current-session observation could be overstated as independent assurance or universal Codex compatibility.
The current project configuration intentionally allow-lists six tools, so the live host cannot prove eight-tool exposure without a separately authorized configuration change.
Configuration inspection could expose private values unless evidence is restricted to tool names, enabled state, bounded timeout facts, and normalized CLI status.
The existing uncommitted parity slice overlaps STATUS.md and must be preserved while the new task changes only its own admitted evidence section.
Official OpenAI documentation establishes Codex MCP configuration and filtering behavior but does not independently prove AgentGov tool semantics.
Reviewed assumption: The current Codex session is a real MCP consumer for the project-scoped AgentGov server.
Reviewed assumption: The active callable AgentGov tool inventory is the host surface available to this Agent in the current session.
Reviewed assumption: The prior parity changes remain user-owned, uncommitted, and excluded except for the shared current-status surface.
Reviewed assumption: The resolved alignment journey remains available for the required post-change native self-review.
Reviewed unknown: Whether a fresh Codex session with an eight-tool allow-list would expose and successfully call completion and drift review remains unproven.
Reviewed unknown: Cross-host compatibility, repeated reliability, adoption, causal incident reduction, and business benefit remain unknown.

title: Record live Codex MCP consumer binding evidence
